plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. Early and mid-season cultivars open in winter, brightening gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak winter)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe's mild coastal regions and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea. In Japan, camellias are associated with samurai because the flower drops whole instead of shedding petals.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pinkish tones, with golden stamens at the center. It flowers through snow and frost in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens.
plants.location: Native to the mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; cultivated in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family. All parts of the plant are toxic, and it was historically used in folk medicine with dangerous results.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: Not actually in bloom in the north, but in the Southern Hemisphere summer, relatives like Lampranthus and Delosperma carpet slopes in daisy-like blooms. This low succulent has fleshy leaves and vivid magenta flowers that open in strong sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape and Lesotho highlands; cultivated in Australia, New Zealand and dry regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The flowers close on cloudy days and at night, and the succulent leaves have glistening bladder cells that look like ice crystals, giving the plant its name.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous plant with tall, sturdy stalks bearing several huge trumpet-shaped flowers. It is a famous winter bloomer indoors in the Northern Hemisphere and also blooms outdoors in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; outdoors in mild climates in winter to spring
plants.location: Parent species native to the tropical Andes and Brazil; grown worldwide as a potted holiday plant and in frost-free gardens
plants.funFact: Bulbs can be forced into bloom in about 6 to 8 weeks, and a single large bulb can send up several flower stalks in one season.
